cards.front: What index identifies the first C# array element?
For an array of length n, what is its last valid index?
Why is using i <= array.Length risky in a loop?
cards.back: It tries to access index Length, outside valid bounds.

cards.front: What does an array initializer do?
cards.back: Supplies initial element values when creating the array.
The number of elements allocated in the array.
Visiting each array element without explicitly managing an index.

cards.front: Why choose for instead of foreach when changing positions by index?
cards.back: A for loop gives explicit control of indices and traversal order.
Inspecting elements in sequence until a match is found or values are exhausted.

cards.front: What sentinel index can represent a failed array search?
cards.back: -1, because valid array indices are nonnegative.
Arrays whose corresponding indices represent related fields of one record.

cards.front: If an int array element is passed by value, can a method reassign the original element through its parameter?
cards.back: No; reassignment changes only the copy.

cards.front: Can a method receiving an array parameter modify its elements?
cards.back: Yes; caller and callee can reference the same array object.

cards.front: Is an array argument automatically the same as a ref parameter?
cards.back: No. The array reference is copied by value unless the parameter itself is declared ref.

cards.front: Can a C# method return an array?
cards.back: Yes; the return value is a reference to an array object.

cards.front: When is a sequential search appropriate?
cards.back: When checking elements one at a time, including unsorted data.

cards.front: What precondition does binary search normally require?
cards.back: Data sorted according to the comparison order.
